rows.label: Annual deaths from pesticide suicide (Sri Lanka)
rows.explainer:
"However, pesticide self-poisoning is still the second most common method of suicide in Sri Lanka, causing 800 to 1000 deaths for each of the last 3 years according to official statistics [13]. Most recent data suggested that the incidence of pesticide suicide in rural Sri Lanka remains around 20/100,000 population [14] – far higher than the global incidence of suicide from all means [1] Many of these deaths occur after ingestion of pesticides classified by the WHO as being of only moderately acute toxicity [15], due to the large volumes ingested and the solvents in these agricultural formulations [16, 17]."

Weerasinghe et al. 2020, p. 2: https://bmcpublichealth.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12889-020-08871-7

rows.label: Adjustment for change in pesticide suicide without intervention (OK)
Annual deaths from pesticide suicide (Nepal)
rows.explainer:
We have not prioritized vetting these figures in depth. In some cases we rely on estimates provided to us by the Centre for Pesticide Suicide Prevention. CPSP worked with the Central Police Forensic Science Laboratory and local hospitals to collect toxicology data on the pesticides used in suicides between April 14, 2019 and February 12, 2020. They identified 891 suicide deaths. We apply two adjustments: (i) multiplying by 365/304 to annualize the estimate, and (ii) multiplying by 1.2 to account for likely underreporting of pesticide suicides. We have not thoroughly investigated (ii), but expect it is likely that toxicology is not completed for every poisoning death. Because we are uncertain about (ii), we apply only a small adjustment.

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1dlowXW5Yz2hqjBrFMCVYnzj3acCbgDgzD5gzPI7oxNg/edit#gid=153469866

rows.label: Adjustment for recent pesticide bans (Nepal)
rows.explainer: Nepal and India have recently banned a number of HHPs. This adjustment accounts for those bans. We have not fully reviewed the state of recent pesticide bans in other countries, but apply a small adjustment to account for pesticide bans we don't know about.

rows.label: No effect (Nepal)
rows.explainer: These are very uncertain forecasts, informed by CPSP's past impact. They are intended to reflect the additional percentage point probability that CPSP contributes to pesticides being banned. GiveWell is early in its work in public health regulation, and we expect these forecasts to be miscalibrated. We hope to develop better intuitions for the likelihood of success of this kind of work as we gain experience in the area.

Annual deaths from pesticide suicide (Regional (Global))
rows.explainer:
We have not prioritized vetting these figures in depth. In some cases we rely on estimates provided to us by the Centre for Pesticide Suicide Prevention. "We estimate that both WHO and FAO staff will be engaged with 5-15 countries each year to support their reduction of pesticide suicides and HHP use." 

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Fn4jS4x_0l3zDUkv64ohSatRDqXzz89v/edit

"There are currently around 160,000 pesticide suicides every year. We want to get these numbers down to <16,000 within 5-10 years.

"Of these deaths, we estimate that 50,000 occur in China, 70,000 in
India, and 40,000 elsewhere in the world."

Email from Michael Eddleston, October 15 2020 (unpublished)

My very uncertain best guess is that CPSP will be able to engage with countries comprising ~25% of the remaining burden of 40,000 through its regional work.

rows.label: Adjustment for recent pesticide bans (Regional (Global))
rows.explainer: Nepal and India have recently banned a number of HHPs. This adjustment accounts for those bans. We have not fully reviewed the state of recent pesticide bans in other countries, but apply a small adjustment to account for pesticide bans we don't know about.

rows.label: No effect (Regional (Global))
rows.explainer:
These are very uncertain forecasts, informed by CPSP's past impact. They are intended to reflect the additional percentage point probability that CPSP contributes to pesticides being banned. GiveWell is early in its work in public health regulation, and we expect these forecasts to be miscalibrated. We hope to develop better intuitions for the likelihood of success of this kind of work as we gain experience in the area. Estimates for CPSP's global and regional work are particularly uncertain, and these may be substantial over- or underestimates.

We haven't done more to make these estimates more accurate because (a) we largely assessed these funding gaps qualitatively, and (b) CPSP's work would be cost-effective according to this model even if the global work had no impact.

rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for research, technical assistance and policy work: mostly people. Our judgment; we haven't seen this grant's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Researchers and advisers could typically earn considerably more in consulting or industry. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
